Role and task instructions:
You are writing a eulogy for your brother, Jason Wilson, who passed away last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center, at age 67.

User request:
You have been entrusted with the honor of delivering a eulogy for Jason Wilson, a beloved brother, friend, and community member. Your task is to write a speech that captures the essence of Jason's life, celebrates his legacy, and provides comfort to the diverse group of mourners gathered to bid him farewell. Jason deceased at age 67, last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center.
Your audience will include family members, friends, colleagues, and acquaintances from Jason's life. They are a mix of various ages and backgrounds, united in their grief and respect for Jason. Your speech should resonate with this diverse group, bringing them together in remembrance and celebration of Jason's life.

answer:
Thank you all for being here to remember my brother, Jason Wilson. To our family, his friends, his colleagues, and everyone who came to know him through this community: your presence means more than I can say.

Jason passed away last Tuesday at Oakwood Medical Center. He was 67 years old. It is difficult to speak those words and understand that they belong to someone who has been part of my life for so long.

For me, losing Jason means losing someone who belongs to my earliest understanding of family. A brother is part of the story you tell about where you came from. Whatever changes as you grow older, that connection remains. Jason will always be part of my story, and I will always be grateful that he was my brother.

I will miss being able to speak to him. I will miss the conversations I thought we still had time to have. And I know that each of you will feel his absence in your own way—in a familiar place, during an ordinary day, or at a moment when you find yourself wanting to tell him something.

Each person here knew Jason through a different relationship. Some of you shared a lifetime with him. Some knew him through friendship, through work, or through the community. You carry memories that others here may never have heard. Together, those memories help us remember the fullness of his life.

That is something I find comforting today: there is more of Jason to remember than any one of us could hold alone.

Sixty-seven years cannot fit into a few minutes of speaking. There were ordinary days and important milestones, private experiences and shared occasions. Today, even as we mourn his death, we honor all those years of living. We honor the relationships he formed and the place he held in so many lives.

In the days ahead, I hope we will keep telling his stories. Tell the ones that make you smile. Share the small details you remember—the things that might seem too ordinary to mention, but that bring him clearly to mind. Those details will be precious to those of us who loved him.

And as we remember Jason, let us take care of one another.

There is no single way we need to feel today. Some of us may want to talk; others may need quiet. Tears may come unexpectedly. So may laughter. There is room for all of it here. We do not have to find perfect words or make this loss easier than it is. Sometimes simply sitting beside someone is enough.

To everyone who has offered kindness, reached out, or come here today: thank you. You remind our family that we have people to turn to as we learn to live with Jason’s absence.

Jason, I wish we had more time. I love you, and I will miss you. I am grateful for the history we shared and for the simple, lasting privilege of calling you my brother.

Goodbye, Jason. You have a place in our family and in our hearts that will always be yours.
